Subject: Private deployment intake — network evidence & KMS questions

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We want to keep momentum on getting our private deployment scheduled for the week of Aug 21. To make sure our security/compliance team has what they need, can you confirm the minimal network artifacts Redwood requires to validate the environment? Specific asks from our side: 

- A sample service account principle and required IAM roles for the provisioning step
- KMS integration checklist (customer KMS vs Redwood-managed keys)
- Firewall port list and egress destinations your installers talk to during provisioning
- Any required DNS records or SRV entries for telemetry/health checks

I'll attach our current network diagram and we can map gaps on your side. If you can outline a short mutual action plan (MAP) we can circulate to our security reviewers.

Appreciate it — Paul

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com <olga_petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment intake — network evidence & KMS questions

Paul —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is the short intake summary and the minimal evidence items we need to complete pre-provisioning validation. I've listed ownership for each item so we have clear owners for the MAP: 

1) IAM/service accounts (owner: Borealis)
   - Service account used for deployment with roles: ComputeAdmin (provisioner), KMSCryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter (if using customer KMS), StorageObjectAdmin (artifact staging).
   - Evidence: service-account JSON (or equivalent role binding screenshots) + policy doc.

2) KMS choices (owner: joint)
   - Option A: Customer-managed KMS (recommended for regulated workloads). We need key ARN/ID and admin contact.
   - Option B: Redwood-managed keys (simpler — will require data-at-rest attestation).
   - Evidence: key policy snippet + rotation window.

3) Network & firewall (owner: Borealis)
   - Required egress to: api.redwood-inference.com (443), 52.23.*/18 (provisioning pool CIDR), monitoring.redwood-inference.com (443).
   - Ports: 443 outbound, 22 inbound (optional, jumpbox), NTP 123 UDP to pool NTP servers if locked down.
   - Evidence: FW rule exports (CSV) and VPC peering/route table exports.

4) DNS & TLS (owner: Borealis)
   - We require CNAMEs for service discovery only if customer-managed hostnames are desired. TLS certs can be customer-provided or Redwood-provisioned via ACME.

5) Telemetry & audit (owner: joint)
   - Audit log forwarding endpoints and retention window.

Next steps (proposed MAP):
- Aug 03: Borealis provides network diagram + service account role export (Paul)
- Aug 06: Redwood reviews diagram, returns annotated diagram + gap list (Olga)
- Aug 09: Borealis returns KMS policy and FW rule exports; Redwood confirms final checklist (Ben)
- Aug 11: Pre-provisioning signoff and scheduling

I attached a short template you can paste into your internal ticketing to accelerate evidence collection.

Regards,
Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

Quick notes after reviewing the diagram and KMS sheet: 

- Diagram looks good; there's a missing route for the provisioning pool CIDR in the east-az subnet (Samantha — can you confirm route table export includes the 10.121.0.0/16 route?).
- On service account evidence: we can accept role-binding screenshots and a short statement from your security owner confirming no long-lived keys are present. We will not ask for raw key JSON over email.
- For KMS: if customer-managed, we need a key policy snippet showing Redwoods' service principal has Encrypt/Decrypt permissions. A single redacted snippet is sufficient.

I'll prepare an annotated diagram with the provisioning endpoints highlighted and upload it to the Drive folder by EOD. Once we have the firewall CSV and the route table export, we can mark "network validated" and book provisioning.

Ben
